3.  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report
  State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within 30 days following each
  fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment balances.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt the resolution accepting the FY24-25 Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report.

4.  City Manager Employment Agreement
  On November 16, 2021, the City Council appointed David Maistros as City Manager to
  the City of Avalon for a three-year term. The contract was executed on December 16,
  2021 for a three-year term beginning on February 1, 2022. After the closed session of the
  January 21, 2025 regular City Council Meeting, the City Attorney reported that the City
  Council had unanimously authorized a new agreement for the City Manager.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize execution of the Employment Agreement for City Manager Services with
  David Maistros.

5.  Los Angeles County Public Health Services Contract
  The City of Avalon contracts with Los Angeles County Department of Health to provide
  public health services. These services include enforcement of any orders, or regulations
  set by the California Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Code, Title 11.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute the Los Angeles County Public Health Services
  Contract.

6.  Resolution Approving the Blanket Authority to Apply for Grant Funds from the Los
  Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District for Measure A Funding for
  Projects and Programs
  The City of Avalon has received Measure A funds in the past to support the development
  and improvement of the Skate Park, City Park, Kids Park and the picnic area of Lover’s
  Cove. In 2025 the granting agency is implementing a new process to administer funding
  for projects and programs. This process requires the City Council to authorize the City
  Manager, or his designee, to apply for grant funding.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution approving the blanket authority of the City Manager to apply for grant
  funds from the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District for Measure
  A funding for projects and programs.

 7.  2025 Waterside Permit Renewals
  Each year, prior to December, the Harbor Master reviews all existing Waterside Permits.
  If the Harbor Master determines that, because of changed circumstances, a permit should
  not be renewed, or should be renewed on different terms and conditions, he shall forward
  his recommendation to the City Council together with a list of all permits that he
  recommends should be renewed for another term without change.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the Harbor Master to renew Waterside Permits for 2025.

8.  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Planning Consultant
  On March 21, 2023 the City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a
  professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-
  call planning consultant services for a not to exceed contract sum of $125,000 for a one-
  year term with two optional one year renewal terms. On February 20, 2024, the City
  Council authorized the City Manager to renew the agreement for an additional one-year
  term for an annual sum not to exceed $150,000.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a professional services agreement
  with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-call planning consultant services
  for a three-year term for an annual cumulative total not to exceed $150,000.00.

9.  Authorization to Provide On-Site Engineering and Support Services for WWTP Control
  System
  PERC Water maintains the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant and have requested to
  contract The LeMasters Company to improve the control system at the plant. The
  improvements require integration of a new piece of equipment into its existing control
  system to maintain operational efficiency and compliance with regulatory requirements.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize PERC Water to contract The LeMasters Company to provide on-site
  engineering and support services for the control system at the Wastewater Treatment
  Plant from Sewer Fund 108-25-652 1 for an amount of not-to-exceed $71,775.

10.  Global Paving RFP
  The need exists for the City to perform paving repairs throughout the City of Avalon. The
  proposed scope of work for this project will focus on repairing and rehabilitating areas
  impacted by utility cuts and pot holes throughout the City as well as application of a crack
  seal compound. This work will prepare the roads for a more comprehensive city-wide
  slurry seal project. The slurry seal project will be performed by separate procurement
  process. Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee(s) to develop and solicit a request for
  proposals from qualified firms to implement city-wide paving repairs.

11.  Waterside Proect Application Catalina Island Mermaids dba Avalon Barebottoms
  —

  The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application proposing Catalina Island
  Mermaids LLC, dba Avalon Barebottoms, to provide limited dive services to boaters and
  others in Avalon Harbor. The services provided will include boat bottom cleaning,
  underwater maintenance/zinc replacement and underwater search and recovery for lost
  items.
  Recommended Action
  Make the affirmative finding that conditions set forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have
  been met and grant the Waterside Project Application to Catalina Island Mermaids, dba
  Avalon Barebottoms, with the following conditions: 1. Notification will be made to Harbor
  Office Personnel prior to dive operations being conducted. The Harbor Master retains the
  ability to restrict or curtail operations when conditions dictate. 2. Current registration for
  the skiff used in dive operations will be provided to the Harbor Master annually. 3. Skiff
  used in dive operations will be secured to one of the public dinghy docks and meet all
  requirements for use of these docks. 4. Personnel conducting dives will have current and
  applicable professional certifications for dive operations and take all necessary safety
  precautions while operating within the Harbor. 5. Applicant will obtain a business license
  for Avalon Barebottoms separate from Catalina Island Mermaids LLC. This waterside
  permit applies to the conditions of use for Avalon Barebottoms. Activities related to
  Catalina Mermaids will begin and end from the shore. 6. Applicant abides by the Standard
  List of Conditions for Waterside Permit Holders.

12.  Waterside Permit Application Island Enterprises, Inc. dba Catalina Adventure Tours
  —

  In May 2024 Island Enterprises, dba Catalina AdventureTours, transferred in ownership.
  The transfer in ownership did not include transfer of an existing waterside permit. The
  new owners of Island Enterprises submitted a waterside permit application on September
  8, 2024.
  Recommended Action
  Make the affirmative finding that conditions set forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have
  been met and grant the Waterside Project Application to Island Enterprises, dba Catalina
  Tours, contingent upon the following conditions: 1. Allow Island Enterprises to utilize 1
  non-exclusive use float in position “E” on the pier for their tour boat operation, utilizing the
  semisubmersible Nautilus (USCG documentation 1079045). The City will not charge fees
  for the float so long as its use is non-exclusive to Island Enterprises. 2. Allow occasional
  use of the Cabrillo Mole floats to pick up groups as long as Island Enterprises does not
  interfere with cross channel carriers or cruise ship traffic. 3. Require City Council approval
  if Island Enterprises elects to utilize their PUC Tariff on-call charter service to pick up
  passengers in all areas specified on the Tariff excluding services between any vessels,
  points and places starting with and ending within the Avalon city limits. 4. If City Council
  approves at a later date, allow Island Enterprises on-call charters the ability to utilize any
  Green Pier float and allow occasional use of the Cabrillo Mole floats to pick up groups as

  long as Island Enterprises does not interfere with cross channel carriers or cruise ship
  traffic. 5.Require Island Enterprises to pay nightly mooring fees for their vessels.

13.  Waterside Project Change Conditions of Use— Avalon Aquatic Excursions
  The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application to change the conditions of
  use of their waterside permit. Currently, the waterside permit authorizes sightseeing,
  whale and dolphin watching trips, and snorkeling tours. Applicant proposes adding
  passenger transport service to and from White’s Landing utilizing a 30’ U.S. Coast Guard
  inspected vessel with a passenger capacity of 22, which he is in the process of obtaining.
  This vessel will take the place of the 26’ vessel proposed in the original application.
  Recommended Action
  Make the affirmative finding that conditions set forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have
  been met and grant the Waterside Project Application to Avalon Aquatic Excursions, with
  the following conditions: 1. All operations to load nd unload passengers will take place
  on Pleasure Pier floats with occasional use of the floats at the Cabrillo Mole. Applicant
  must not interfere with other commercial boat traffic including cross-town ferry and/or
  cruise ship tender traffic. During summer months applicant will make all efforts to utilize
  the shore-boat float of the End Float of the pier. 2. Applicant abides by the standard list
  of conditions for Waterside Permit holders. 3. Applicant meets all regulatory requirements
  for passenger-carrying vessels of this type, including any U.S. Coast Guard and Public
  Utilities Commission requirements. 4. Prior to vessel acquisition, applicant will provide the
  Harbor Master with the technical specifications, including make, model, length, beam,
  propulsion type, passenger capacity for approval. Any future proposed changes to these
  specifications will require prior Harbor Master approval in writing.

14.  City Vehicle Storage Yard Policy
  Over the years, the City has utilized different mechanisms to address illegal and
  abandoned vehicles within the City limit, including using on island commercial tow
  companies or partnering with mainland tow companies to conduct bi-annual “round-ups.”
  No robust program has existed since before 2019.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the City of Avalon Vehicle Storage Yard Policy.

15.  Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance Repealing and Replacing Title 4, Public
  Safety, Chapter 4-1 Bicycles and Repealing Chapter 4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code
  The City has seen a proliferation of bicycles, electric bicycles, motorized bicycles, electric
  motorcycles, dirt bikes, pocket bikes, scooters, and other unregistered/off-road vehicles.
  Recommended Action
  Introduce and waive all readings of an Ordinance of the City of Avalon Repealing and
  Replacing Title 4, Chapter 4-1 and Repealing Chapter 4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code
  Regarding Bicycles, Electric Bicycles and Motorized Bicycles.

SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt the resolution accepting the FY24-25 Second Quarter
Treasurer’s Report.

REPORT SUMMARY: State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment
balances. Attached is the Second Quarter Treasurer’s Report for FY24-25. The report was
shared with the City Treasurer prior to presentation to City Council.

The purpose of the report is to inform, on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment
balances, the investment types, yields, and market values, and to ensure that the City’s
investments are in compliance with the City’s adopted investment policy. The report shows that
all of the City’s funds are in compliance with its investment policy. In general, operating cash is
held in US Bank checking accounts and any excess cash is invested in California’s Local
Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and various certificates of deposit (CD5). In accordance with
Government Code sections 16429.1 and 53601 et seq., the City cannot invest more than 30%
of its portfolio in CDs. CD5 accounted for 15.7% of the unrestricted cash and investments for
the quarter ended December 31, 2024.

The City reinvested $5.59 million in United States Treasury Bills that had matured during the
quarter into another seven month term. The City also invested in one new CD during the
quarter maturing in 5 years with estimated yields of 4.15%. The City takes a ladder approach
with staggered maturities for its CD investments to balance its goals of high rates in the short-
term with stability to withstand market fluctuations in the longer-term. The City will continue to
assess for opportunities to increase its investment returns while maintaining necessary liquidity
and compliance with its investment policy.

The unrestricted cash balance for the second quarter of 2024-2025 totaled $26.8 million, an
increase of $1.8 million from the second quarter of 2023-2024. The unrestricted cash balance
includes cash from enterprise funds (e.g. Harbor, Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste) not
available for general government functions. The increase in unrestricted cash is partially
attributable to the seasonality of visitor-driven tax revenues and the timing of significant capital
outlays anticipated to increase during the next fiscal year. While the majority of grant funding is
performed on a cash reimbursement basis, the unrestricted cash and investments balance
also includes $2 million in grant pre-funding received in preparation for construction of the
 second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Improvement project that has not been spent as of
December 31, 2024. The unrestricted cash balance increased by $1 .2 million compared to the
first quarter of 2024-2025. The increase in unrestricted cash balance from the prior quarter is
attributable to the timing of property tax and direct assessments for sewer, saltwater and solid
waste services received in late December. The City expects to begin construction on several
major capital projects, including the second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal
rehabilitation and the Five Corners Pedestrian Improvement project, during the next quarter
which will reduce future unrestricted cash balances.

SUBJECT:  City Manager Employment Agreement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize execution of the Employment Agreement for City
Manager Services with David Maistros.

REPORT SUMMARY: On November 16, 2021, the City Council appointed David Maistros as
City Manager to the City of Avalon for a three-year term. The contract was executed on
December 16, 2021 for a three-year term beginning on February 1, 2022.

After the closed session of the January 21, 2025 regular City Council Meeting, the City Attorney
reported that the City Council had unanimously authorized a new agreement for the City
Manager. The agreement includes:

  •  Term of 4 years, expiring January 31, 2029;
  •  Requirement for Annual Evaluations;
  •  Annual salary of up to $247,500 per year, subject to cost of living increase afforded to all
  City employees and potential merit increase at the discretion of the City Council;
  •  Annual administrative leave of 96 hours per year.
  •  Insurance, sick, vacation and other benefits as provided to all management employees
  with a minimum 10 years of service; and
  •  Six months severance, including healthcare benefits, if termination without cause.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Organizational stability.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Budgeted in Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: There will not be an
executed contract for City Manager.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute contract.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon contracts with Los Angeles County Department
of Health to provide public health services. These services include enforcement of any
orders, or regulations set by the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) and Los
Angeles County Code, Title 11.

There is no charge to the City for the enforcement of State, County, or other regulations
outlined in the Avalon Municipal Code; however, the City may be subject to standard fees
assessed for inspection of city-owned facilities. The City may request in writing additional
public health services that are not required by statute, regulation or CDPH Order.
Additional services, if authorized, may be charged to the City at rates approved by the
Board of Supervisors.

The agreement offers an initial term of five (5) years  —  expiring on June 30, 2029  —  with
an automatic five (5) year renewal period.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Public health, welfare and safety.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not
have a contract for public health services.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Provide a copy of the executed agreement to Los Angeles
County.

Conservation Measure (Measure A). Measure A also designates the Los Angeles County
Regional Park and Open Space District (RPOSD) and establishes the Los Angeles
County Board of Supervisors, acting as the RPOSD, as the governing body to administer
Measure A grants.

and improvement of the Skate Park, City Park, Kids Park and the picnic area of Lover’s
Cove.

programs. This process requires the City Council to authorize the City Manager, or his
designee, to apply for grant funding.

SUBJECT:  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Planning Consultant

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a
professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-call
planning consultant services for a three-year term for an annual cumulative total not to exceed
$1 50,000.00.

REPORT SUMMARY: On March 21, 2023 the City Council authorized the City Manager to
execute a professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, [[C
(“Sagecrest”) for on-call planning consultant services for a not to exceed contract sum of
$125,000 for a one-year term with two optional one year renewal terms.

On February 20, 2024, the City Council authorized the City Manager to renew the agreement for
an additional one-year term for an annual sum not to exceed $150,000.

Prior to City Council authorization, the City of Avalon had been seeking technical planning and
environmental review expertise through advertising for a full-time Planning Director position.
However, though a job posting for a vacant Planning Director position had been advertised an
approximate 10 month period, from May 2022 to March 2023, the City had not been able to
identify a candidate.

The agreement with Sagecrest allows the City to utilize a broad range of consultants with
expertise in varying areas of planning, development and land use entitlements.

During Sagecrest’s tenure as the City’s on-call planning consultant, they have provided
significant assistance to staff regarding a myriad of planning and environmental items including,
but not limited to:
  -  Processing of planning entitlement applications, including Conditional Use Permits,
  Tentative Parcel Maps, Site Plan Reviews, and Coastal Development Permits;
  -  Restarting the Local Coastal Program amendment process to address seal level rise and
  climate change planning;
  -  Meeting with prospective planning entitlement/building permit applicants to answer
  planning questions in person, via email and phone;
  -  Regularly reviewing legislation to keep the City up to date on State planning regulations;
  -  Preparing multiple municipal code updates to fulfill the requirements of the reporting for
  the Housing Element Implementation Plan;
   -  Preparing the 2023 General Plan and Housing Element annual reports;
  -  Coordinating with City staff on research into potential updates to the City’s Transient
  Rental Licensing program;
  -  Continuously meeting and conferring with Island Stakeholders regarding potential
  development and land use including, Catalina Island Health.

The cost for services provided by Sagecrest compared to the potential cost of a fully weighted
full-time Planning Director salary ($180,000) results in a significant cost savings to the City.
Additionally, due to Sagecrest’s experience in the field, the City has experienced a significant
cost savings in planning related legal fees.

Due to anticipated increased volume in high level planning items, including multiple large-scale
housing developments, potential hospital construction, and significant potential legislative
changes to the Transient Rental License Ordinance, City staff recommend authorizing the City
Manager to negotiate and execute a contract agreement for a three-year term for $150,000.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Sustainability of operations.

FISCAL IMPACTS: FY 2023-24 Planning Services budget has contract sum budgeted (account
number 10255-5055).

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have
specialized planning support.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  City Vehicle Storage Yard Policy

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Approve the City of Avalon Vehicle Storage Yard Policy.

REPORT SUMMARY: Over the years, the City has utilized different mechanisms to
address illegal and abandoned vehicles within the City limit, including using on island
commercial tow companies or partnering with mainland tow companies to conduct bi
annual “round-ups.” No robust program has existed since before 2019.

With a limited program, the City has seen a proliferation of unregistered and abandoned
motorcycles, scooters, golf carts, and full size vehicles as well as illegal off-road
motorcycles and vehicles being driven on City roadways. Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department (LASD) Avalon station has also repeatedly indicated that the absence of a
tow yard restricts their ability to adequately enforce bicycle and vehicle infractions.

Staff identified an underutilized portion of an existing City-owned property adjacent to the
household hazardous waste drop off-facility as a solution. City staff then met with LASD
staff and LASD tow contractor Kruger Tow to discuss logistics in creating a robust tow
and storage program.

After consulting stakeholders, the vehicle code, and municipal code, a draft policy was
created and shared with City and LASD leadership.

In addition, staff are nearing completion of a City vehicle storage yard for the storage of
full size vehicles, autoettes, motorcycles, and bicycles. Improvements include a concrete
pad, driveway, fencing, gates, lighting, security camera installation, and a metal storage
container for bicycles. All expected to be completed by the end of the month.

The proposed policy includes the process related to operating the vehicle storage yard,
towing, storage, release, disposal, compliance, and training standards.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Introduce and waive all readings of An Ordinance of the
City of Avalon Repealing and Replacing Title 4, Chapter 4-1 and Repealing Chapter 4-
10 of the Avalon Municipal Code Regarding Bicycles, Electric Bicycles and Motorized
Bicycles.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City has seen a proliferation of bicycles, electric bicycles,
motorized bicycles, electric motorcycles, dirt bikes, pocket bikes, scooters, and other
unregistered/off-road vehicles. It has been observed by the community, first responders,
and staff many of the riders are not adhering to basic traffic laws. These infractions
predominantly include, but are not limited to, unsafe speeding, reckless operation, not
wearing a helmet, not meeting age/licensure requirements, and more. These problems
are not unique to Avalon and a challenge for many communities.

The municipal code related to bicycles was last revised in 2001 with many changes to the
California Vehicle Code addressing electric bicycles and motorized bicycles.

Staff conducted research and talked with law enforcement agencies in both Los Angeles
and Orange County, including reviewing updated ordinances in those jurisdictions.
Although many observed violations can be satisfied with a notice to appear and traffic
court, LASD is suggesting modifying the ordinance to allow for the issuance of
administrative citations to help change behavior for first time offenders and Avalon youth.

According to LASD command staff, LASD Avalon station has attempted public outreach,
education, and enforcement programs over the last twelve months to improve traffic
safety to little improvement. City Council has since directed staff to update the municipal
code as an added tool to improve traffic safety, especially for community youth.

The proposed ordinance covers licensing, operation, and enforcement provisions for
bicycles and electric bicycles. Perhaps most notably in the ordinance is the ability for local
law enforcement to securely store bicycles, e-bicycles, and illegal off-road
vehicles/motorcycles for violations of the proposed municipal code amendment. The
 ordinance revisions are in concert with the near completion of the vehicle storage yard. It
maintains those sections concerning skates and skateboards which are in Chapter 4-1

At this time it is also recommended to consolidate existing Chapters 4-1 Bicycles,
Pushmobiles, and Toy Vehicles and 4-10 Bicycles on Public Property of the Avalon
Municipal Code.

bicycles.

Within 10 days after any change in ownership or the dismantling to take out of use any
bicycle, electric bicycle or motorized bicycle registered pursuant to the provisions of this
chapter, the person in whose name such bicycle has been registered shall report such
information to the Vehicle Clerk.

  ARTICLE 3: OPERATIONAL REGULATIONS
§ 4-1-301.  Applicability  of Traffic Laws.
Every person riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorized bicycle upon a street shall
be granted all of the rights and shall be subject to all of the duties applicable to the
driver of a vehicle by the laws of the State pertaining to the rules of the road, or by the
terms of this Code or other ordinances of this City applicable to the driver of a vehicle.

§ 4-1 -302. Obedience to Traffic-Control Devices.
It shall be unlawful for any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle or motorized
bicycle to fail to obey the instructions of official traffic-control signs and other traffic-
control devices applicable to vehicles.

§ 4-1 -303. Method of Riding and Number of Riders.
No person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorized bicycle shall allow more
persons at one time than the number for which such bicycle is designed and equipped.

§ 4-1 -304. Riding on Roadways.

§ 4-1 -306. Speed.
No person shall operate a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorized bicycle at a speed
greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing, and in no
event at a speed which endangers the safety of persons or property. No operator shall
travel over 20 miles per hour.

§ 4-1 -307. Emerging from Entering Alley, Driveway, Bicycle Path.
The operator of a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorized bicycle emerging from an alley,
driveway, bicycle path, building or otherwise approaching upon a sidewalk or sidewalk
area shall yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians on such sidewalk or sidewalk area,
and upon entering a roadway, shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles or bicycles on
the roadway.

§ 4-1 -308. Parking.
No person shall leave a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorized bicycle lying on its side on
any sidewalk, nor upon the public right-of-way or the sidewalk rack to support the
bicycle or against a building or at a curb, except in such a manner as to afford the least
obstruction to pedestrian traffic.

§ 4-1.309. Sidewalks.
It shall be unlawful for any person to ride or operate any bicycle, electric bicycle, or
motorized bicycle on any sidewalk.

§ 4-1 -310. Equipment.
A person shall not tamper with or modify a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorized bicycle,
so as to change the speed capability of such bicycle, unless they appropriately replace

§ 4-1 -311. Age and Licensing Restrictions.
  (a) A person riding an electric, or motorized bicycle is subject to the same provisions
  as a person riding a bicycle, as described in Article 4 of Chapter 1 of Division 11,
  commencing with Section 21200 of the California Vehicle Code. A rider must be
  16 years of age or older to operate a Class 3 electric bicycle. A person under the
  age of 18 must wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet when riding an
  electric bike on a public roadway, bikeway, bicycle path, bicycle trail, or bicycle
  route regardless of electric bicycle class. All people operating or riding as a
  passenger upon a Class 3 electric bicycle shall comply with Section 21213 of the
  California Vehicle Code regarding the wearing of a properly fitted and fastened
  bicycle helmet.

  (b) A driver license with an M-1 or M-2 endorsement, registration, vehicle insurance,
  and a Department of Transportation (DOT) compliant helmet is required when
  operating a motorized bicycle. Motorized bicycles shall be operated in
  accordance with all applicable provisions of the California Vehicle Code and are
  not permitted on any bicycle path, trail, playground, park, school ground, or open
  space area in the City.

§ 4-1 -401. Enforcement.
  (a) Responsibility of parent. The parent of any child, and the guardian of any ward,
  shall not authorize or knowingly permit any minor child or ward to violate any of
  the provisions of this division.
  (b) In addition to any other penalty authorized by law, any violation of this section
  shall constitute an infraction, and may be enforced pursuant to Chapter 1-9.

§ 4-1 -402. Storage for Violation of Law.
Any bicycle, electric bicycle, motorized bicycle, or off-highway vehicle is subject to being
towed and stored at the owner’s expense for any violation of this chapter until the owner
is compliant with the provisions of this chapter and the California Vehicle Code are
complied with. Property retained by the City of Avalon or Los Angeles County Sheriff’s

§ 4-1.403. Removal from Public Property.
A seven-day notice of intent to remove will be attached to any bicycle, electric bicycle,
motorized bicycle, or off-highway vehicle which is parked at a public facility for three or
more consecutive days beyond the length of time permitted. The notice shall be mailed,
by registered mail, to the last registered owner of such bicycle, unless the bicycle is
unregistered or is in such condition that identification numbers are not available to
determine ownership. If such bicycle is not removed within seven days of the mailing
and/or posting of the notice of intent to remove, the City may remove and store such
bicycle as provided in § 4-1 .402. Neither the City nor a contractor thereof shall be liable
for damage caused to a bicycle or a part thereof, or to any security device connected to
the public property, by removal pursuant to this section.

§ 4-1.404. Recovery and Storage
The owner of any bicycle, electric bicycle, motorized bicycle, or off-highway vehicle
found, stored, or recovered, which is stored by the City or its agents, shall be charged
daily storage fees and/or release fee in an amount to be set by resolution of the City
Council. Prior to release of bicycles, electric bicycles, and motorized bicycles, the owner
shall pay the storage fees and apply for and receive a license pursuant to the provisions
of § 4-1.201. Prior to the release of off-highway vehicles, the owner shall pay the
storage fees and sign a waiver of liability on a form approved by the City Attorney.
